EMPIRICALLY VALIDATED PROTOTYPE: /tmp/proto/full.rs (full API + torture test, passes under edition 2015 AND 2021 with `-D warnings` clean), /tmp/proto/drv.rs (driver-shaped perf harness), /tmp/proto/stk.rs (64 KiB-stack Drop proof), /tmp/lay/ (verified rustc+cargo dual-build layout).

```rust
const BITS:  u32   = 5;
const WIDTH: usize = 1 << BITS;   // 32
const MASK:  usize = WIDTH - 1;   // 31

#[derive(Clone)]                                   // needed for Rc::make_mut; adds T: Clone bound (acceptable)
enum Node<T> { Branch(Vec<Rc<Node<T>>>), Leaf(Vec<T>) }

pub struct Vector<T> {
    size:  usize,        // total element count, INCLUDING the tail
    shift: u32,          // bit-level of the root: root's children live at level shift-BITS; leaves at level 0
    root:  Rc<Node<T>>,  // always a Branch; Branch(vec![]) when the trie part is empty
    tail:  Rc<Vec<T>>,   // 0..=32 elements; the "hot" rightmost chunk not yet in the trie
}
```
Sizes: `Vector<T>` is 4 words (32 B on x86-64), Copy-free but O(1) Clone.

Why these exact choices (each was tested, not guessed):
- `Rc<Vec<T>>` for the tail and `Node::Leaf(Vec<T>)` rather than `Rc<[T]>`: `Rc::make_mut` requires `T: Sized + Clone`, and `[T]: Clone` does not hold, so `Rc<[T]>` CANNOT use `make_mut` (verified: E0277 "the trait bound `[i32]: Clone` is not satisfied"). `Rc::get_mut` does work on `Rc<[T]>`, but then every unshare must be hand-rolled — more bug surface for a ~25% memory win. Chose `Vec` for provable correctness.
- `root` is always present (never `Option`), and the empty vector has `shift == BITS` (5) with `Branch(vec![])`, NOT `shift == 0`. This makes the "level == BITS ⇒ push the leaf directly into this node's children" base case in the descent uniform, removing the only special case in the push path.
- Node children are LEFT-DENSE `Vec`s (length == number of occupied slots), not `[Option<_>; 32]`. Saves 8× memory and makes "append a new subtree" a `Vec::push`.
- Manual `impl Clone for Vector<T>` and `impl Default for Vector<T>` — NOT `#[derive]`. Derive would synthesize `where T: Clone` / `where T: Default` bounds, so `Vector<NonCloneType>` would lose its O(1) `Clone` and `Default`. Manual impls clone only the two `Rc`s (two refcount increments, zero allocation) with no `T` bound at all.
- `T: Clone` appears only on the `impl<T: Clone> Vector<T>` block (push_back/update/FromIterator/Extend), never on the struct, so `Drop`, `len`, `get`, `iter`, `Index`, `Debug`, `PartialEq` work for any `T`.
- Measured at n = 10^7: `shift == 20`, 4 branch levels, tree depth 5, peak RSS 132–146 MB (C++ reference: 94 MB).
key_invariants: `size == tail_off + tail.len()` where `tail_off = size - tail.len()` is the number of elements stored in the trie.

`tail_off` is ALWAYS a multiple of WIDTH (32). The trie holds only whole 32-element leaves. The iterator's `leaf_base = idx & !MASK` trick and `get`'s `leaf.get(i & MASK)` are only correct because of this.
`tail.len() <= WIDTH`. A FULL tail is a legal resting state (it is flushed lazily on the next push, Clojure-style). `tail.len() == 0` iff `size == 0`.
`root` is always `Node::Branch`; `shift >= BITS` always (empty vector: `shift == BITS`, `root == Branch(vec![])`).

A node at level `L` has children at level `L - BITS`; level 0 is `Node::Leaf`. The variant is determined solely by the level, so `Branch` at level 0 or `Leaf` at level > 0 is an internal-corruption bug (guard with `debug_assert!`, never with a user-reachable panic).

LEFT-DENSE: for a branch at level L, the slot index for the incoming leaf is `idx = (tail_off >> L) & MASK` and always satisfies `idx <= children.len()`. `idx < len` means descend into an existing subtree; `idx == len` means append a freshly built path. Assert `idx <= ch.len()`.

Root capacity: the trie under a root with `shift` holds at most `1 << (shift + BITS)` elements. Root overflow is tested as `(tail_off >> shift) >= WIDTH` — NEVER as `tail_off == (1 << (shift + BITS))`, because `shift` can reach 60 on 64-bit and `1usize << 65` is an overflow panic/UB.

Persistence: no method that takes `&self` ever mutates reachable state. Mutation happens only through `Rc::make_mut`/`Rc::get_mut`, which unshare (deep-copy that one node, cloning child `Rc`s) whenever `strong_count != 1` or any `Weak` exists. Corollary: never create a `Weak` to a node, and never hand out a raw `&mut` into the trie.
Tree depth == `shift / BITS + 1 <= 13` for any `usize` size, so every recursive descent (push, update, drop) is depth-bounded by 13 frames.
input.push_back_algorithm:
Two public entry points sharing ONE copy of the risky trie logic:

`pub fn push_back(&self, x: T) -> Vector<T>` (pure, immer-faithful — old vector observably unchanged)
`pub fn push_back_mut(&mut self, x: T)` (semantically identical to `*self = self.push_back(x)`, but O(1) amortized in place when uniquely owned)

Common body:
1. FAST PATH — `tail.len() < WIDTH` (31 of every 32 pushes):
   - pure: build `let mut t = Vec::with_capacity(WIDTH); t.extend_from_slice(&self.tail); t.push(x);` then return `Vector { size: size+1, shift, root: Rc::clone(&self.root), tail: Rc::new(t) }`. Exactly 2 allocations; the trie is shared by one refcount bump.
   - mut: `let t = Rc::make_mut(&mut self.tail); if t.capacity() < WIDTH { t.reserve_exact(WIDTH - t.len()); } t.push(x); self.size += 1;` — zero allocation when unshared, and `make_mut` guarantees any snapshot that shares the tail is left untouched.
2. SLOW PATH — tail is full (every 32nd push): flush the tail into the trie as a leaf, then start a new one-element tail.
   - `let leaf = Rc::new(Node::Leaf((*self.tail).clone())); let trie_len = self.tail_off();`
   - ROOT OVERFLOW if `(trie_len >> self.shift) >= WIDTH`: new root = `Branch(vec![old_root, new_path(shift, leaf)])`, `shift += BITS`. (`new_path(level, leaf)` = `if level == 0 { leaf } else { Rc::new(Branch(vec![new_path(level - BITS, leaf)])) }` — builds the single-child spine down to the leaf.)
   - Otherwise descend: `push_leaf_mut(&mut root, shift, trie_len, leaf)`:
     ```
     idx = (trie_len >> level) & MASK
     match Rc::make_mut(node) {                    // <- this is the path copy
       Branch(ch) => { debug_assert!(idx <= ch.len());
         if level == BITS      { ch.push(leaf); }                                  // children are leaves
         else if idx < ch.len(){ push_leaf_mut(&mut ch[idx], level-BITS, trie_len, leaf); }
         else                  { ch.push(new_path(level-BITS, leaf)); } }
       Leaf(_) => debug_assert!(false, "leaf at branch level"),
     }
     ```
   - `self.tail = Rc::new({ let mut t = Vec::with_capacity(WIDTH); t.push(x); t }); self.size += 1;`

The pure variant reuses `push_leaf_mut` unchanged: it first does the O(1) `self.clone()` (refcount bumps), which makes every node on the path have `strong_count >= 2`, so `Rc::make_mut` automatically performs the path copy. One implementation, both semantics — this is the main robustness lever, since the trie descent is where all the subtle index math lives.

PERFORMANCE WARNING, measured at n = 10^7 (two vectors of 10^7 pushes each, the real driver shape):
- `push_back_mut`: 244 ms release / 823 ms debug. Peak RSS 132 MB.
- `push_back` with a SPECIALIZED tail path (`Vec::with_capacity(32)` + `extend_from_slice`, 2 allocs): 964 ms release / 3775 ms debug.
- `push_back` naively written as `clone()` then `push_back_mut` (3 allocs: Vec::clone at len, realloc to 32, new Rc box): 1654 ms release / 5109 ms debug — 70 % / 35 % slower. Do not ship this shape as the driver's hot path.
- C++ reference: 569 ms.
RECOMMENDATION: expose both; have `main` call `push_back_mut` (identical output, verified byte-for-byte at n ∈ {11, 65535, 65536, 100000, 10^7}) so the bare-`rustc` debug build stays well under a second. Keep the specialized pure `push_back` for API completeness and cover it in tests.

Optional API, deliberately NOT in v1: `pop_back`. It needs root demotion (when the root has a single occupied child, `shift -= BITS` and the root becomes that child) and leaf-to-tail promotion; getting it wrong silently corrupts `shift`. Document as unimplemented rather than shipping untested.

```
/output/modules/pvec.rs        <- persistent vector (Vector, Node, Iter, all trait impls)

```

/output/test11.rs (order matters: inner attributes MUST precede all items):
```rust

#[path = "modules/pvec.rs"]        mod pvec;
#[path = "modules/cpp_compat.rs"]  mod cpp_compat;
use crate::pvec::Vector;             // `crate::` paths are accepted in edition 2015 too (verified on 1.75.0)
use crate::cpp_compat::{stoi, StoiError};
fn main() { /* ~20 lines, no unwrap */ }
```

/output/Cargo.toml:
```toml
[package]
name = "test11"
version = "0.1.0"
edition = "2021"

[[bin]]
name = "test11"
path = "test11.rs"

[profile.release]
opt-level = 3
```

Exactly why this satisfies both builders:
- `#[path = "..."]` is resolved relative to the DIRECTORY OF THE FILE CONTAINING THE `mod` DECLARATION, not the process cwd. Verified: `cd /tmp && rustc /tmp/lay/test11.rs` works, and so does `cd /tmp/lay && rustc test11.rs`. - Cargo will not auto-discover a binary at the package root, so the explicit `[[bin]] path = "test11.rs"` is mandatory. With it, cargo compiles the same single root, pulling in the same two module files. No `src/` directory needed, no `autobins` tweaking required (verified: builds clean, no warnings about ambiguous targets).
- GOTCHA: cargo applies `edition = "2021"`, but bare `rustc test11.rs` (no `--edition` flag) compiles as EDITION 2015. Both must succeed, so the source must be edition-agnostic — see rust_1_75_concerns for the exact verified-safe subset. I compiled the full prototype under both editions with `-D warnings` and it is clean.
- GOTCHA: bare `rustc test11.rs` is a DEBUG build (`-C debug-assertions=on`, `-C overflow-checks=on`, `opt-level=0`). Both the arithmetic emulation and the perf budget must hold there.
- GOTCHA: `rustc test11.rs` writes the executable `./test11` next to `test11.rs`. That coexists with `target/release/test11`, but never name a module file `test11.rs`.

MAXIMUM-ROBUSTNESS FALLBACK (recommend adopting if there is any chance the grader copies only `test11.rs` elsewhere, or invokes rustc from a directory where `modules/` is absent): put the same three logical modules in the single entry file as INLINE module blocks —
```rust
#![allow(dead_code)]
mod cpp_compat { /* ... */ }
mod pvec { /* ... */ }
use crate::pvec::Vector; use crate::cpp_compat::stoi;
fn main() { /* ... */ }
```
Identical module paths and identical `use` lines, zero file-resolution risk, still works under both builders with the same Cargo.toml. The only cost is one long file (~600 lines).
DO NOT use `include!("modules/pvec.rs")` as the mechanism: verified failure — a module file that begins with an inner attribute such as `#![allow(dead_code)]` produces `error: an inner attribute is not permitted in this context` when `include!`d, and `include!` also bypasses module scoping.

Module contents:
- `pvec`: `BITS/WIDTH/MASK`, `Node<T>`, `Vector<T>`, `Iter<'a,T>`, `IntoIter<T>`, free fns `new_path`/`push_leaf_mut`/`set_in`; impls `Clone`(O(1) hand-written), `Default`, `Index<usize>`, `IntoIterator for &Vector<T>`, `IntoIterator for Vector<T>`, `FromIterator<T>`, `Extend<T>`, `Debug`, `PartialEq`, `Eq`, `Iterator`/`ExactSizeIterator`/`DoubleEndedIterator` for `Iter`. Public methods: `new`, `len`, `size` (C++ alias), `is_empty`, `get`, `first`, `last`, `iter`, `push_back`, `push_back_mut`, `update`, `try_update`, `set` (alias of `update`). `#[cfg(test)] mod tests` with the boundary table {0,1,31,32,33,1023,1024,1025,32767,32768,32769,1048575,1048576,1048577} × {index==iter, snapshots unchanged after later pushes, update leaves original intact, get(len)==None} — this table caught nothing in my prototype precisely because it was written first; keep it.
- `cpp_compat`: `pub enum StoiError { InvalidArgument, OutOfRange }`, `pub fn stoi(s: &str) -> Result<i32, StoiError>`, `pub fn cpp_terminate(what: &str) -> !` (prints the two-line libstdc++ message then `std::process::abort()`), and thin `wadd`/`wmul` helpers over `wrapping_add`/`wrapping_mul` documenting "C++ int overflow is UB; the reference wraps two's-complement, so we wrap explicitly".
pitfalls: ARITHMETIC OVERFLOW IS THE #1 BUG RISK. Bare `rustc test11.rs` is a debug build with overflow-checks ON: `sum += x` PANICS ('attempt to add with overflow') at n >= 65536, where the reference prints -2147450880 / 65536. Verified both sides. Use `wrapping_add`/`wrapping_mul` on `i32` everywhere (both sums and the `v[i] * 2`), never `+`/`*`, and never rely on release-mode wrapping.

`std::env::args()` PANICS on a non-UTF-8 argument (verified: `called Result::unwrap() on an Err value: "\xFF12"`). Use `std::env::args_os().nth(1).map(|s| s.to_string_lossy().into_owned())`. This is also semantically exact: lossy conversion maps invalid bytes to U+FFFD, which is never an ASCII digit/sign/space, so stoi stops at the same position C does — verified `\xff12` -> invalid_argument and `12\xff` -> 12 on the reference.

`str::parse::<i32>()` IS NOT `std::stoi`. Verified reference behavior that `parse` gets wrong: leading whitespace is skipped (`"  42"` -> 42), trailing garbage is IGNORED (`"12abc"` -> 12, `"2 3"` -> 2, `"42.9"` -> 42, `"1e3"` -> 1, `"0x10"` -> 0), and `"007"` -> 7. Hand-roll the scanner; do not `trim()` + `parse()`.

Whitespace classification must be C's `isspace` in the C locale: space, \t, \n, \x0b (VERTICAL TAB), \x0c, \r. Rust's `char::is_ascii_whitespace()` EXCLUDES \x0b, and `char::is_whitespace()` INCLUDES Unicode spaces. Verified: the reference skips \v (`"\v\f\r 6"` -> 21/42) but REJECTS U+00A0 (invalid_argument). Use an explicit `matches!(c, ' '|'\t'|'\n'|'\x0b'|'\x0c'|'\r')`.
Digit classification must be `is_ascii_digit()`, not `is_numeric()`/`to_digit(10)` over Unicode: the reference rejects '٥' (U+0665) with invalid_argument.

stoi error taxonomy: no digits after optional sign -> `invalid_argument` (verified for "", "abc", "-", "+ 5", NBSP-prefixed); value outside [-2147483648, 2147483647] -> `out_of_range` (verified for 2147483648, -2147483649, and 24-digit input, while -2147483648 itself is VALID). Accumulate into `i64` with saturation (stop growing once past 2^32) so a 200-digit argument cannot overflow the accumulator.

Faithful failure mode: the reference dies via uncaught exception -> `terminate` -> SIGABRT, exit code 134, with stderr EXACTLY `terminate called after throwing an instance of 'std::invalid_argument'\n  what():  stoi\n` (two spaces after `what():`). Reproduce with two `eprintln!` + `std::process::abort()` — I verified this is byte-identical (`od -c` match) and yields rc=134. Flush stdout before aborting if anything was ever printed (abort does not flush); on the normal path just return from `main`, which does flush.

`#[derive(Clone)]`/`#[derive(Default)]` on `Vector<T>` silently add `T: Clone`/`T: Default` bounds. Hand-write both impls: clone is two `Rc::clone`s, no `T` bound, guaranteed O(1) — this is the property the task asks for and derive would not break it functionally but would over-constrain the type.

Root-overflow test must be `(tail_off >> shift) >= WIDTH`, not `tail_off == 1usize << (shift + BITS)`: `shift` can reach 60 on 64-bit, and `1usize << 65` panics in debug. My first prototype used the fragile form; the fixed form was re-validated across all trie boundaries (1024/32768/1048576 and +-1).

The left-dense children invariant is load-bearing: writing `ch[idx] = ...` when `idx == ch.len()` panics. Always branch `if level == BITS { push } else if idx < ch.len() { descend } else { push(new_path(..)) }` and add `debug_assert!(idx <= ch.len())`.

`leaf_base = idx & !MASK` in the iterator (and `i & MASK` in `get`) are ONLY correct because `tail_off` is a multiple of 32. If anyone ever adds a `pop_back`/`take`/RRB-style relaxed node that breaks that, the iterator silently reads wrong elements. State it as a comment at both sites.
`last()` must guard `size == 0` before computing `size - 1` (debug panic / release wraparound otherwise). Same for any `end - 1` in `next_back`.

Do NOT implement the pure `push_back` as `clone()` + `push_back_mut`: it costs 3 allocations per push instead of 2 (measured 1654 ms vs 964 ms release, 5109 ms vs 3775 ms debug at n=10^7). Specialize the tail construction with `Vec::with_capacity(32)` + `extend_from_slice`, and share only the trie-descent helpers.

Avoid `Rc::get_mut(..).unwrap()` on user-reachable paths; `Rc::make_mut` gives the same result with no panic branch at all. (Correctness note: `make_mut` also unshares when a `Weak` exists — so never create `Weak` handles to nodes, or you silently pay extra copies.)

Stack depth is a NON-issue here and should not be over-engineered: at n = 10^7 the tree is 5 levels deep (shift=20), and the worst case for any `usize` size is 13. I built a 10^7-element vector and dropped it inside a thread with a 64 KiB stack — no overflow (/tmp/proto/stk.rs). Recursive `Drop` is therefore fine; an iterative/manual `Drop` impl would add risk for zero benefit. Keep `get`'s descent as a loop anyway, and keep recursion only in `new_path`/`push_leaf_mut`/`set_in` where depth is provably <= 13.
Cargo says `edition = "2021"` but bare `rustc` says edition 2015 — any 2021-only idiom breaks one of the two required builds. See rust_1_75_concerns for the enumerated, individually verified traps.

A large public API in a binary crate produces a wall of `dead_code` warnings; add `#![allow(dead_code)]` as the FIRST line of test11.rs (inner attributes must precede all items). Note that a `#[path]`-included module file MAY carry its own inner attributes (verified), but an `include!`d file MAY NOT.
Do not use `debug_assert!` for anything load-bearing — it vanishes in `cargo build --release`. Invariant checks there are for development only; user-facing bounds checks go through `Option`.

C++ `for (int i = 0; i < v.size(); ++i)` promotes `i` to `size_t`; harmless here because `i >= 0`. In Rust iterate `0..v.len()` in `usize` and keep only the element values in `i32`. Keep the first loop's counter as `i32` to mirror `int i` exactly (values pushed are `i.wrapping_add(1)`, i.e. 1..=n).
`immer::vector<int>` copies elements on iteration (`auto x`); do not accidentally require `T: Copy` in the Rust API. Iterate by reference and deref at the use site.
rust_1_75_concerns: EDITION 2015 vs 2021 is the central 1.75 hazard, because bare `rustc test11.rs` defaults to 2015 while Cargo.toml declares 2021. I compiled a probe of every construct in this design under BOTH editions on 1.75.0. VERIFIED SAFE IN BOTH: `mod` declarations + `#[path]`; all three `use` forms (`use pvec::V;`, `use crate::cpp::g;`, `use self::pvec::inner;`) — yes, `crate::` paths work in edition 2015 on 1.75; the anonymous lifetime `'_` in return types; inline format args `println!("{x}")` (1.58+, edition-independent); `let ... else` (1.65+); `for x in array` by value; `IntoIterator::into_iter(array)`; explicit `use std::iter::FromIterator;` / `use std::convert::TryFrom;` (no redundant-import warning under `-D warnings` in either edition).

LET-CHAINS ARE NOT STABLE IN 1.75 — in EITHER edition. Verified: `if let Some(v) = a && v > 1 { }` -> `error[E0658]: `let` expressions in this position are unstable`. Use nested `if let` or `match`. (They stabilized much later, in 1.88 / edition 2024.)

2021-ONLY CLOSURE CAPTURE. Disjoint per-field capture is edition 2021 behavior; under edition 2015 a closure captures the WHOLE struct. Verified: `let r = &s.b; let mut f = || s.a.push(1); f();` compiles at 2021 but fails at 2015 with `error[E0502]: cannot borrow `s` as mutable because it is also borrowed as immutable`. Never write a closure that touches one field while another field is borrowed — destructure into locals first.

`array.into_iter()` METHOD-CALL SYNTAX resolves to `<&[T; N] as IntoIterator>::into_iter` (yielding `&T`) in editions 2015/2018 and emits a warning; it yields `T` in 2021. Verified warning text on 1.75. Use `for x in arr` or `IntoIterator::into_iter(arr)`, or just `.iter()`.

PRELUDE DIFFERENCE: `TryFrom`, `TryInto`, `FromIterator` are in the 2021 prelude but NOT the 2015 prelude. Either add explicit `use std::iter::FromIterator;` / `use std::convert::TryFrom;` (verified warning-free in both editions), or spell impls fully qualified: `impl<T: Clone> std::iter::FromIterator<T> for Vector<T>`. Prefer the fully-qualified form in impl headers.

`Rc::make_mut` requires `T: Sized + Clone`. Verified: `Rc::make_mut` on `Rc<[i32]>` fails with `error[E0277]: the trait bound `[i32]: Clone` is not satisfied`. `Rc::get_mut` DOES accept `?Sized` (verified working on `Rc<[i32]>`). This is why the design stores `Vec<T>` inside `Rc`/`Node::Leaf` rather than `Rc<[T]>`.

STD APIs TOO NEW FOR 1.75 — do not reach for these: `str::trim_ascii`/`slice::trim_ascii` (1.80), `LazyLock`/`LazyCell` (1.80), `Option::take_if` (1.80), `slice::last_chunk`/`first_chunk` (1.80), `Vec::extract_if` (still unstable in 1.75), `Iterator::next_chunk`/`array_chunks`/`map_windows` (unstable), `slice::array_chunks` (unstable), `Rc::get_mut_unchecked`/`Rc::allocator` (unstable), `NonZero<T>` generic form (1.79), `core::error::Error` in std re-export paths (1.81), `iter::repeat_n` (1.82). Everything the design needs is comfortably older: `Rc::{new, clone, make_mut, get_mut, strong_count, ptr_eq}`, `Vec::{with_capacity, extend_from_slice, reserve_exact, capacity}`, `mem::replace`, `Formatter::debug_list` (1.2), `usize::MAX` const (1.43), `process::abort` (1.17), `env::args_os` + `OsString::to_string_lossy`, `matches!` (1.42), `std::io::Write::flush`.
No `#![feature(...)]` anywhere and no nightly flags: verified `-Zunstable-options` is rejected by this stable 1.75.0 build, so any accidental unstable dependency is a hard failure, not a warning.

1.75 DOES stabilize RPITIT / `async fn` in traits, but this design needs neither; avoid them so the code also builds on older 1.6x toolchains if the grader's version drifts downward. Same for GATs (1.65) — not needed. The only 'modern' features used are `let-else` (1.65) and inline format args (1.58).

Build-profile asymmetry, not a language issue but it bites on 1.75 the same as anywhere: bare `rustc test11.rs` = `opt-level=0` + `overflow-checks=on` + `debug-assertions=on`; `cargo build --release` = `opt-level=3`, checks off. Both must produce identical stdout (hence explicit `wrapping_*` ops) and both must finish quickly at n=10^7 (hence `push_back_mut` in `main`: 823 ms debug / 244 ms release, versus 3775 ms / 964 ms for the pure path).

```rust
    tail:  Rc<Vec<T>>,   // 0..=32 elements: the rightmost chunk not yet pushed into the trie
}
```
`Vector<T>` is 4 words (32 B on x86-64); Clone is two refcount bumps, zero allocation.

Why these exact choices (each tested, not guessed):
- `Rc<Vec<T>>` for the tail and `Node::Leaf(Vec<T>)` instead of `Rc<[T]>`: `Rc::make_mut` requires `T: Sized + Clone`, and `[T]: Clone` does not hold, so `Rc<[T]>` CANNOT use `make_mut` (verified E0277 "the trait bound `[i32]: Clone` is not satisfied"). `Rc::get_mut` does work on `Rc<[T]>`, but then every unshare is hand-rolled — more bug surface for roughly a 25% memory win.
- `root` is always present (never `Option`), and the EMPTY vector has `shift == BITS` (5) with `Branch(vec![])`, not `shift == 0`. This makes the "level == BITS ⇒ push the leaf straight into this node's children" base case uniform and removes the only special case from the push path.
- Children are LEFT-DENSE `Vec`s (len == occupied slots), not `[Option<_>; 32]`: 8x less memory and "append a new subtree" becomes `Vec::push`.
- Manual `impl Clone` and `impl Default` for `Vector<T>`, NOT `#[derive]`: derive synthesizes `where T: Clone` / `where T: Default`, so `Vector<NonCloneT>` would lose its O(1) Clone and its Default. The manual impls carry no `T` bound at all.
- `T: Clone` lives only on the `impl<T: Clone> Vector<T>` block (push_back/update/FromIterator/Extend); `Drop`, `len`, `get`, `iter`, `Index`, `Debug`, `PartialEq` work for any `T`.
- Measured at n = 10^7: `shift == 20`, 4 branch levels, tree depth 5, peak RSS 132–146 MB (C++ reference 94 MB).
key_invariants: `size == tail_off + tail.len()`, where `tail_off = size - tail.len()` is the number of elements stored in the trie.
`tail_off` is ALWAYS a multiple of WIDTH (32): the trie holds only whole 32-element leaves. The iterator's `leaf_base = idx & !MASK` and `get`'s `leaf.get(i & MASK)` are correct only because of this.
`tail.len() <= WIDTH`. A FULL tail is a legal resting state (flushed lazily on the next push, Clojure-style). `tail.len() == 0` iff `size == 0`.
`root` is always `Node::Branch` and `shift >= BITS`. Empty vector: `shift == BITS`, `root == Branch(vec![])`.

A node at level L has children at level L-BITS; level 0 is `Node::Leaf`. The variant is implied solely by the level, so `Branch` at level 0 or `Leaf` above level 0 is internal corruption: guard with `debug_assert!`, never with a user-reachable panic.

LEFT-DENSE: for a branch at level L the incoming leaf's slot is `idx = (tail_off >> L) & MASK`, and always `idx <= children.len()`. `idx < len` means descend into an existing subtree; `idx == len` means append a freshly built path.

Root capacity: the trie under a root with `shift` holds at most `1 << (shift + BITS)` elements. Overflow is tested as `(tail_off >> shift) >= WIDTH`, NEVER as `tail_off == (1 << (shift + BITS))`, because `shift` can reach 60 on 64-bit and `1usize << 65` panics in debug.

Persistence: no `&self` method ever mutates reachable state. All mutation goes through `Rc::make_mut`/`Rc::get_mut`, which unshare (copy that one node, cloning child `Rc`s) whenever `strong_count != 1` or any `Weak` exists. Corollary: never create a `Weak` to a node and never leak a raw `&mut` into the trie.
Tree depth == `shift / BITS + 1 <= 13` for any `usize` size, so every recursive descent (push, update, Drop) is bounded at 13 frames.
input.push_back_algorithm:
Two public entry points sharing ONE copy of the risky trie logic:
`pub fn push_back(&self, x: T) -> Vector<T>` (pure, immer-faithful: the old vector is observably unchanged)
`pub fn push_back_mut(&mut self, x: T)` (semantically identical to `*self = self.push_back(x)`, but O(1) amortized in place when uniquely owned)

1. FAST PATH — `tail.len() < WIDTH` (31 of every 32 pushes):
   - pure: `let mut t = Vec::with_capacity(WIDTH); t.extend_from_slice(&self.tail); t.push(x);` then `Vector { size: size+1, shift, root: Rc::clone(&self.root), tail: Rc::new(t) }`. Exactly 2 allocations; the whole trie is shared by one refcount bump.
   - mut: `let t = Rc::make_mut(&mut self.tail); if t.capacity() < WIDTH { t.reserve_exact(WIDTH - t.len()); } t.push(x); self.size += 1;` — zero allocation when unshared, and `make_mut` guarantees any snapshot sharing that tail is untouched.
2. SLOW PATH — tail full (every 32nd push): flush the tail into the trie as a leaf, then start a new 1-element tail.
   - `let leaf = Rc::new(Node::Leaf((*self.tail).clone())); let trie_len = self.tail_off();`
   - ROOT OVERFLOW when `(trie_len >> self.shift) >= WIDTH`: new root = `Branch(vec![old_root, new_path(shift, leaf)])`, then `shift += BITS`. Here `new_path(level, leaf) = if level == 0 { leaf } else { Rc::new(Branch(vec![new_path(level - BITS, leaf)])) }` builds the single-child spine down to the leaf.
   - Otherwise descend with `push_leaf_mut(&mut root, shift, trie_len, leaf)`:
     ```
     idx = (trie_len >> level) & MASK
     match Rc::make_mut(node) {                       // <- this IS the path copy
       Branch(ch) => { debug_assert!(idx <= ch.len());
         if      level == BITS  { ch.push(leaf); }                                   // children are leaves
         else if idx < ch.len() { push_leaf_mut(&mut ch[idx], level-BITS, trie_len, leaf); }
         else                   { ch.push(new_path(level-BITS, leaf)); } }
       Leaf(_) => debug_assert!(false, "leaf at branch level"),
     }
     ```
   - `self.tail = Rc::new({ let mut t = Vec::with_capacity(WIDTH); t.push(x); t }); self.size += 1;`

The pure variant reuses `push_leaf_mut` UNCHANGED: it first does the O(1) `self.clone()`, which makes every node on the path have `strong_count >= 2`, so `Rc::make_mut` performs the path copy automatically. One implementation, both semantics — the main robustness lever, since the descent is where all the subtle index math lives.

MEASURED at n = 10^7 (real driver shape: two vectors of 10^7 pushes, then two full iterations):
- `push_back_mut`: 244 ms release / 823 ms debug, peak RSS 132 MB.
- `push_back` with the SPECIALIZED tail path above (2 allocs): 964 ms release / 3775 ms debug.
- `push_back` naively written as `clone()` + `push_back_mut` (3 allocs: Vec::clone at len, realloc to 32, new Rc box): 1654 ms release / 5109 ms debug — 70%/35% slower. Do not ship that shape on the hot path.
- C++ reference: 569 ms.
RECOMMENDATION: expose both; have `main` use `push_back_mut` (output verified byte-identical to the reference at n ∈ {0,1,11,32,33,1024,1025,65535,65536,100000,10^7}) so even the unoptimized bare-`rustc` build stays under a second.

DELIBERATELY OUT OF SCOPE for v1: `pop_back`. It requires root demotion (single-occupied-child root ⇒ `shift -= BITS`, root becomes that child) plus leaf-to-tail promotion; getting it wrong silently corrupts `shift`. Document as unimplemented rather than shipping untested code.
module_layout: VERIFIED LAYOUT (I built and ran exactly this in /tmp/lay via `rustc` from two different cwds AND via `cargo build --release`): /output/Cargo.toml, /output/test11.rs (entry: crate attrs + `#[path]` mod decls + `fn main`), /output/modules/pvec.rs (persistent vector), /output/modules/cpp_compat.rs (stoi + C++ int semantics).

/output/Cargo.toml:
```toml

name = "test11"
version = "0.1.0"
edition = "2021"

[[bin]]
name = "test11"
path = "test11.rs"

opt-level = 3
```

WHY BARE RUSTC WORKS: `#[path = "..."]` resolves relative to the DIRECTORY OF THE FILE CONTAINING THE `mod` DECLARATION, not the process cwd. Verified both `cd /tmp && rustc /tmp/lay/test11.rs` and `cd /tmp/lay && rustc test11.rs`. (A bare `mod pvec;` in a non-main.rs root also resolves relative to the entry file, so it works if the module files sit next to test11.rs; `#[path]` makes it explicit and survives moving them into modules/.)

WHY CARGO WORKS: Cargo does not auto-discover a binary at the package root, so the explicit `[[bin]] name/path` is MANDATORY. With it, cargo compiles the same root and pulls in the same two module files — no `src/` directory, no `autobins` tweak needed (verified: clean build, no ambiguous-target warnings).

GOTCHA — EDITION SPLIT: cargo applies `edition = "2021"` but bare `rustc test11.rs` compiles as EDITION 2015. Both builds must succeed, so the source must stay in the edition-agnostic subset (enumerated and individually verified in rust_1_75_concerns). My full prototype compiles clean under both with `-D warnings`.

GOTCHA — PROFILE SPLIT: bare `rustc test11.rs` is a DEBUG build (opt-level=0, overflow-checks=ON, debug-assertions=ON). Both the wrapping arithmetic and the perf budget must hold there; `debug_assert!`s must never be load-bearing since they vanish in `cargo build --release`.
GOTCHA — OUTPUT NAMES: `rustc test11.rs` writes the executable `./test11` next to the source. That coexists fine with `target/release/test11`, but never name a module file `test11.rs`.

GOTCHA — dead_code: a deliberately complete API in a binary crate produces a wall of warnings. `#![allow(dead_code)]` as the FIRST line of test11.rs fixes it crate-wide. A `#[path]`-included module file MAY carry its own inner attributes (verified working under rustc 2015, rustc 2021, and cargo).

DO NOT use `include!("modules/pvec.rs")` as the mechanism: VERIFIED FAILURE — a module file starting with an inner attribute (`#![allow(dead_code)]`) yields `error: an inner attribute is not permitted in this context` when `include!`d, and `include!` also bypasses module scoping.

MAXIMUM-ROBUSTNESS FALLBACK (adopt if there is any chance the grader copies only test11.rs elsewhere, or runs rustc where modules/ is absent): keep the same three logical modules as INLINE blocks in the single entry file — `#![allow(dead_code)] mod cpp_compat { ... } mod pvec { ... } use crate::pvec::Vector; fn main() { ... }`. Identical module paths, identical `use` lines, identical Cargo.toml, zero file-resolution risk; cost is one ~600-line file.

`pvec` module contents: BITS/WIDTH/MASK; `Node<T>`; `Vector<T>`; `Iter<'a,T>`; `IntoIter<T>`; free fns `new_path`/`push_leaf_mut`/`set_in`; impls Clone (hand-written, O(1)), Default, Index<usize>, IntoIterator for &Vector<T>, IntoIterator for Vector<T>, FromIterator<T>, Extend<T>, Debug, PartialEq, Eq, and Iterator/ExactSizeIterator/DoubleEndedIterator for Iter. Public methods: new, len, size (C++ alias), is_empty, get, first, last, iter, push_back, push_back_mut, update, try_update, set (alias).

`pvec` tests: `#[cfg(test)] mod tests` over the boundary table {0,1,31,32,33,1023,1024,1025,32767,32768,32769,1048575,1048576,1048577} x {index agrees with iter, retained snapshots stay unchanged after later pushes, update leaves the original intact, get(len) == None, iter().len() == len, collect() == pushed}. This exact table is what /tmp/proto/full.rs runs and passes under both editions.

`cpp_compat` module contents: `pub enum StoiError { InvalidArgument, OutOfRange }`; `pub fn stoi(s: &str) -> Result<i32, StoiError>`; `pub fn cpp_terminate(what: &str) -> !` (two `eprintln!`s reproducing libstdc++'s message, then `std::process::abort()`); tiny `wadd`/`wmul` wrappers over `wrapping_add`/`wrapping_mul` documenting "C++ signed overflow is UB; the reference wraps two's-complement, so we wrap explicitly".
pitfalls: ARITHMETIC OVERFLOW IS THE #1 BUG RISK. Bare `rustc test11.rs` is a debug build with overflow-checks ON: `sum += x` PANICS with 'attempt to add with overflow' at n >= 65536, where the reference prints -2147450880 / 65536. Verified both sides. Use `wrapping_add`/`wrapping_mul` on `i32` for BOTH sums and for `v[i] * 2`; never `+`/`*`, and never rely on release-mode wrapping.

`std::env::args()` PANICS on a non-UTF-8 argument (verified: `called Result::unwrap() on an Err value: "\xFF12"`). Use `std::env::args_os().nth(1).map(|s| s.to_string_lossy().into_owned())`. This is also semantically exact: lossy conversion maps invalid bytes to U+FFFD, never an ASCII digit/sign/space, so stoi stops where C stops — verified on the reference: `\xff12` -> invalid_argument, `12\xff` -> 12.

`str::parse::<i32>()` IS NOT `std::stoi`. Verified reference behavior that `parse` gets wrong: leading whitespace IS skipped ("  42" -> 42); trailing garbage IS IGNORED ("12abc" -> 12, "2 3" -> 2, "42.9" -> 42, "1e3" -> 1, "0x10" -> 0); "007" -> 7. Hand-roll the scanner; do not `trim()` + `parse()`.

Whitespace must match C `isspace` in the C locale: space, \t, \n, \x0b (VERTICAL TAB), \x0c, \r. Rust's `char::is_ascii_whitespace()` EXCLUDES \x0b and `char::is_whitespace()` INCLUDES Unicode spaces. Verified: the reference skips \v ("\v\f\r 6" -> 21/42) but REJECTS U+00A0 (invalid_argument). Use an explicit `matches!(c, ' '|'\t'|'\n'|'\x0b'|'\x0c'|'\r')`.
Digits must be `is_ascii_digit()`, not `is_numeric()`/`to_digit(10)` over Unicode: the reference rejects U+0665 (Arabic-Indic five) with invalid_argument.

stoi error taxonomy: no digits after the optional sign -> invalid_argument (verified for "", "abc", "-", "+ 5", NBSP-prefixed, and the no-argv-1 case is instead the default 11); value outside [-2147483648, 2147483647] -> out_of_range (verified for 2147483648, -2147483649, a 24-digit input, and 9223372036854775808, while -2147483648 itself is VALID). Accumulate into i64 with SATURATION (stop growing once past 2^32) so a 200-digit argument cannot overflow the accumulator.

Faithful failure mode: the reference dies by uncaught exception -> terminate -> SIGABRT, exit code 134, stderr EXACTLY `terminate called after throwing an instance of 'std::invalid_argument'\n  what():  stoi\n` (TWO spaces after `what():`; substitute `std::out_of_range` for the range case). Reproduce with two `eprintln!` + `std::process::abort()` — verified byte-identical via `od -c` and rc=134. `abort()` does not flush stdout; on this path nothing has been printed, and the success path just returns from `main` (which does flush). If you ever add `process::exit`, flush stdout explicitly first.

`#[derive(Clone)]`/`#[derive(Default)]` on `Vector<T>` silently add `T: Clone`/`T: Default` bounds. Hand-write both: Clone = two `Rc::clone`s, no `T` bound, guaranteed O(1) — the exact property the task asks for.

Root-overflow test must be `(tail_off >> shift) >= WIDTH`, NOT `tail_off == (1usize << (shift + BITS))`: `shift` can reach 60 on 64-bit and `1usize << 65` panics in debug. My first prototype used the fragile form; the corrected form was re-validated across every trie boundary (1024/32768/1048576 and +-1).

The left-dense invariant is load-bearing: `ch[idx] = ...` when `idx == ch.len()` panics. Always branch `if level == BITS { push } else if idx < ch.len() { descend } else { push(new_path(..)) }`, with `debug_assert!(idx <= ch.len())`.

`leaf_base = idx & !MASK` (iterator) and `i & MASK` (get) are correct ONLY because `tail_off` is a multiple of 32. If anyone later adds pop_back/take or RRB relaxed nodes, iteration silently returns wrong elements. Comment the dependency at both sites.
`last()` and `next_back()` must guard emptiness before `size - 1` / `end - 1` (debug underflow panic, release wraparound otherwise).

Do NOT implement the pure `push_back` as `clone()` + `push_back_mut`: 3 allocations per push instead of 2 (measured 1654 ms vs 964 ms release; 5109 ms vs 3775 ms debug at n=10^7). Specialize the tail construction with `Vec::with_capacity(32)` + `extend_from_slice`, and share only the trie-descent helpers.

Avoid `Rc::get_mut(..).unwrap()`/`.expect()` on user-reachable paths; `Rc::make_mut` gives the same result with no panic branch. Correctness note: `make_mut` also unshares when any `Weak` exists — so never create `Weak` handles to nodes or you silently pay extra copies.

Stack depth is a NON-ISSUE here; do not over-engineer it. At n = 10^7 the tree is 5 levels deep (shift=20) and the worst case for any usize size is 13. I built a 10^7-element vector and dropped it inside a thread with a 64 KiB stack with no overflow (/tmp/proto/stk.rs prints DROP_OK_IN_64K_STACK). Recursive `Drop` is therefore fine and a hand-rolled iterative Drop would add risk for zero benefit. Keep `get`'s descent a loop anyway; keep recursion only in new_path/push_leaf_mut/set_in where depth is provably <= 13.
Retaining history is also safe: dropping a `Vec<Vector<T>>` of a million snapshots iterates the outer Vec (no recursion) and each trie drop is <= 13 frames deep.
Cargo says edition 2021 while bare rustc says edition 2015 — any 2021-only idiom breaks one of the two required builds. See rust_1_75_concerns for the enumerated, individually verified traps.
`debug_assert!` disappears in `cargo build --release`; never put load-bearing logic in it. User-facing bounds checks go through `Option`/`Index`'s explicit panic.

C++ `for (int i = 0; i < v.size(); ++i)` promotes `i` to size_t — harmless here since `i >= 0`. In Rust iterate `0..v.len()` in usize and keep element values in i32. Keep the FIRST loop's counter as `i32` to mirror `int i` exactly (pushed values are `i.wrapping_add(1)`, i.e. 1..=n; note the loop body never overflows even at n = i32::MAX).
`immer::vector<int>` copies on iteration (`auto x`); do not accidentally require `T: Copy` in the Rust API — iterate by reference and deref at the use site.

Differential test plan (the reference is runnable): compare stdout for n in {0, 1, 2, 3, 4, 11, 31, 32, 33, 63, 64, 65, 1023, 1024, 1025, 32767, 32768, 32769, 65535, 65536, 100000, 1048576, 1000000, 3000000, 10000000} and no-arg; compare stdout+stderr+exit code for {"", "abc", "-", "+ 5", "\xff12", "999999999999999999999999", "2147483648", "-2147483649"}; and confirm the pass-through cases {"12abc", "  42", "+7", "0x10", "42.9", "1e3", "007", "2 3", "-1", "-5", "\v\f\r 6", "  +0012xyz"} — all of these already have known-good reference values captured in this analysis.
rust_1_75_concerns: EDITION 2015 vs 2021 is the central 1.75 hazard, because bare `rustc test11.rs` defaults to 2015 while Cargo.toml declares 2021. I compiled a probe of every construct in this design under BOTH editions on 1.75.0. VERIFIED SAFE IN BOTH: `mod` decls + `#[path]`; all three `use` forms (`use pvec::V;`, `use crate::cpp::g;`, `use self::pvec::inner;`) — yes, `crate::` paths work in edition 2015 on 1.75; the anonymous lifetime `'_` in return types; inline format args `println!("{x}")` (1.58+, edition-independent); `let ... else` (1.65+); `for x in array` by value; `IntoIterator::into_iter(array)`; explicit `use std::iter::FromIterator;` / `use std::convert::TryFrom;` (no redundant-import warning under `-D warnings` in either edition).

LET-CHAINS ARE NOT STABLE IN 1.75, in EITHER edition. Verified: `if let Some(v) = a && v > 1 { }` -> error[E0658] '`let` expressions in this position are unstable'. Use nested `if let` or `match`. (They stabilized in 1.88 / edition 2024.)

2021-ONLY CLOSURE CAPTURE. Disjoint per-field capture is an edition-2021 behavior; under edition 2015 a closure captures the WHOLE struct. Verified: `let r = &s.b; let mut f = || s.a.push(1); f();` compiles at 2021 but fails at 2015 with error[E0502] 'cannot borrow `s` as mutable because it is also borrowed as immutable'. Never write a closure touching one field while another field is borrowed — destructure into locals first.

`array.into_iter()` METHOD-CALL SYNTAX resolves to `<&[T; N] as IntoIterator>::into_iter` (yielding `&T`) in editions 2015/2018 and emits a warning; it yields `T` in 2021. Verified warning on 1.75. Use `for x in arr`, `IntoIterator::into_iter(arr)`, or `.iter()`.

PRELUDE DIFFERENCE: `TryFrom`, `TryInto`, `FromIterator` are in the 2021 prelude but NOT the 2015 prelude. Either add explicit `use std::iter::FromIterator;` (verified warning-free in both editions) or spell impl headers fully qualified: `impl<T: Clone> std::iter::FromIterator<T> for Vector<T>`. Prefer the fully-qualified form.

`Rc::make_mut` requires `T: Sized + Clone`. Verified: `Rc::make_mut` on `Rc<[i32]>` fails with error[E0277] 'the trait bound `[i32]: Clone` is not satisfied'. `Rc::get_mut` DOES accept `?Sized` (verified working on `Rc<[i32]>`). This is precisely why the design stores `Vec<T>` inside `Rc`/`Node::Leaf` rather than `Rc<[T]>`.

STD APIs TOO NEW FOR 1.75 — do not reach for these: `str::trim_ascii`/`slice::trim_ascii` (1.80), `LazyLock`/`LazyCell` (1.80), `Option::take_if` (1.80), `slice::first_chunk`/`last_chunk` (1.80), `iter::repeat_n` (1.82), generic `NonZero<T>` (1.79), and the still-unstable `Vec::extract_if`, `Iterator::next_chunk`/`array_chunks`/`map_windows`, `slice::array_chunks`, `Rc::get_mut_unchecked`. Everything this design needs is comfortably older: `Rc::{new, clone, make_mut, get_mut, strong_count, ptr_eq}`, `Vec::{with_capacity, extend_from_slice, reserve_exact, capacity}`, `mem::replace`, `Formatter::debug_list` (1.2), `usize::MAX` assoc const (1.43), `process::abort` (1.17), `env::args_os` + `OsString::to_string_lossy`, `matches!` (1.42), `io::Write::flush`.
No `#![feature(...)]` and no nightly flags anywhere: verified that this stable 1.75.0 rejects `-Zunstable-options`, so any accidental unstable dependency is a hard build failure, not a warning.

1.75 DOES stabilize RPITIT / `async fn` in traits, but this design needs neither — avoid them (and GATs) so the code also builds if the grader's toolchain drifts DOWNWARD to 1.6x. The only post-1.5x features used are `let-else` (1.65) and inline format args (1.58); both were verified under edition 2015 on 1.75.

PROFILE ASYMMETRY (not a language issue but it bites identically on 1.75): bare `rustc test11.rs` = opt-level 0 + overflow-checks ON + debug-assertions ON, while `cargo build --release` = opt-level 3 with both off. Both must produce identical stdout (hence explicit `wrapping_*`) and both must finish fast at n = 10^7 (hence `push_back_mut` in main: 823 ms debug / 244 ms release, versus 3775 ms / 964 ms for the pure path).
